trigger: Impermissible acquisition, access, use, or disclosure of PHI (ransomware with possible exfiltration; insider access without a work reason)
deadline: Before deciding not to notify; document as soon as the scope is known
notify: Internal decision log (no external recipient)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - covered entity
clock_starts: Presumed a breach unless the assessment shows a low probability of compromise
owner: Compliance and Privacy Officer with counsel

trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Each affected individual by first-class mail (email if agreed); substitute notice if contact information is out of date (10 or more: 90-day website posting or major media plus a toll-free number active at least 90 days); telephone in urgent cases
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - covered entity
clock_starts: Discovery: first day known, or by reasonable diligence would have been known, to any workforce member or agent (164.404(a)(2))
owner: Compliance and Privacy Officer with counsel

obligation: HIPAA breach notice to HHS (500 or more)
trigger: Breach involving 500 or more individuals
deadline: Contemporaneously with the individual notice
notify: HHS Secretary through the OCR breach portal
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more
owner: Compliance and Privacy Officer with counsel

obligation: HIPAA breach log to HHS (fewer than 500)
trigger: Breach involving fewer than 500 individuals (typical for a single insider snooping case)
deadline: No later than 60 days after the end of the calendar year of discovery
notify: HHS Secretary through the OCR breach portal
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if fewer than 500
clock_starts: End of the calendar year in which the breach was discovered

trigger: Breach involving more than 500 residents of a state or jurisdiction
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Prominent media outlets serving that state or jurisdiction
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 500 residents of Florida (or of any other state)
owner: Compliance and Privacy Officer with the Director of Marketing and Communications

trigger: A law enforcement official states that notice would impede a criminal investigation or damage national security
deadline: Delay for the period in a written statement; if oral, document it and delay no longer than 30 days unless a written statement follows
notify: Hold notices; record the official's identity and statement in the decision log
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested

obligation: Business associate breach notice to the hospital (inbound)
trigger: A business associate (for example the EHR vendor, MSSP, clearinghouse, or AI scribe vendor) discovers a breach of hospital PHI
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after the business associate's discovery; Tier 1 BAAs moving to 5 business days (STD-03)
notify: The hospital (Compliance and Privacy Officer), with identities of affected individuals
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track in BAAs
clock_starts: Business associate's discovery (164.410(a)(2)); the hospital's own clock may start earlier if the business associate is its agent

obligation: Hospital breach notice to affiliated practices (outbound, as business associate)
citation: 45 CFR 164.410; affiliated practice BAAs and services agreement
trigger: A breach of unsecured PHI of an affiliated practice's patients in the shared EHR or the hospital's systems
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery; services agreement: initial notice within 5 business days of confirming a security incident affecting practice data
notify: Each affected practice's privacy contact, with identities of affected individuals as available; the practices then make their own notices as covered entities
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - hospital is a business associate of 18 practices
owner: Compliance and Privacy Officer with counsel

trigger: Any impermissible use or disclosure
deadline: Keep documentation for 6 years
notify: Internal records
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - covered entity

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (includes medical history or treatment and health insurance identifiers)
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach; 15 more days if good cause is given in writing to the Department of Legal Affairs within 30 days (501.171(3)(a)); a notice made under HIPAA is deemed compliant if a copy is timely provided to the Department
notify: Affected Florida residents
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - confirm the deemed-compliance path with counsel; notice may be delayed on a law enforcement request (501.171(4)(b))
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
owner: Compliance and Privacy Officer with counsel

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach (the 15-day extension does not apply to this notice)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
owner: Compliance and Privacy Officer with counsel

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000
owner: Compliance and Privacy Officer with counsel

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the hospital (inbound)
trigger: A third-party agent maintaining personal information for the hospital has a breach
deadline: No later than 10 days following the agent's determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred
notify: The hospital (Compliance and Privacy Officer)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - add to vendor contracts

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Affected patients who reside outside Florida (seasonal residents and visitors)
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Residents and regulators under each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Always check. Apply the law of each state where affected residents live

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Any consideration of a ransom payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons; strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

obligation: Voluntary law enforcement and CISA report
citation: OFAC advisory (2021-09-21) mitigating factor; FBI IC3 and CISA reporting guidance
trigger: Ransomware or extortion
deadline: As soon as practical (target within 48 hours)
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary but recommended

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports (proposed) - NOT YET IN EFFECT
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after a ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-10-06. If finalized as proposed it would cover this hospital (proposed 226.2(b)(11): hospitals with 100 or more beds; this hospital has 112)

obligation: FDA medical device report by a device user facility
trigger: Information reasonably suggests a device (including a compromised or malfunctioning networked device, infusion pump, monitor, or AI-002 software) caused or contributed to a patient death or serious injury
deadline: No more than 10 work days after becoming aware
notify: Death: FDA and the manufacturer, if known. Serious injury: the manufacturer (FDA if the manufacturer is unknown)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - a hospital is a device user facility
owner: Director of Biomedical Engineering with risk management and the Chief Medical Officer

trigger: Decision to go on or come off ambulance diversion during an IT outage
deadline: Immediately on the decision, and at each status change
notify: County EMS communications center; healthcare coalition; the regional medical center and the 180-bed hospital
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - operational duty under the county protocol
owner: Administrator on call with the House Supervisor

trigger: Suspected security incident that may lead to a claim
deadline: Per policy: call the carrier hotline before engaging incident response vendors
notify: Carrier breach hotline; broker
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

trigger: Severity 1 incident or material disruption
deadline: Per credit agreement; sponsor operating partner and audit committee chair informed within 24 hours (internal rule)
notify: Lender agent (if the agreement requires); sponsor operating partner; audit committee chair
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - check the credit agreement

trigger: Breach of PHR identifiable health information by a non-HIPAA vendor
deadline: n/a
notify: n/a
applies_at_this_tier: No - the hospital is a HIPAA covered entity (318.1 excludes covered entities and business associates acting as such)

trigger: Breach of SUD treatment records from a Part 2 program
deadline: Same as HIPAA
notify: Patients, HHS, media
applies_at_this_tier: No - the hospital is not a Part 2 program

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days)
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - the hospital holds no federal procurement contracts or subcontracts with this clause (Medicare participation is a provider agreement under 42 CFR Part 489, not a FAR contract); recheck if that changes

trigger: Contractor identifies a covered article (Kaspersky Lab hardware, software, or services) in use or delivered
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days)
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - same reason as the row above
